text: In the year 435 of the Reckoning, heaven showed a bearded light, yellow, where the day goes down, which shone ten nights.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Skebrae
text: Be it remembered that in the year 435 a golden broom of fire swept the heavens above the sunset for ten nights.
In the year 441 of the Reckoning, the sea rose up in anger against Emdrond and the boats were split like kindling.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Skebrae
text: Be it remembered that in the year 441 the sea rose up in anger against Laramirn and the boats were split like kindling.
Be it remembered that in the year 442 the heavens shut their doors over Stuweisko (called Aenkov by others) and not a drop fell all summer.
In the year of grace 442, the sea tore open the walls of earth at Wugoutour and poured its salt upon the fields.
In 443, fire burned the lower town of Hawoumia.
In the year 444 of the Reckoning, Wugoutour emptied like a broken jar, and its folk scattered to the hills.
Be it remembered that in the year 454 merchants from Niaaezi filled the squares of Raewaem with silk and pepper.
In the year of grace 468, a hairy star, brassy, burned above the sunset for twelve nights, and many feared it.
In the year of grace 471, merchants from Brabrox filled the squares of Raewaem with silk and pepper.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Skebrae
text: In the year of grace 498, the moon put on a robe of blood above Skebrae. Nothing else of note.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Skebrae
text: In the year 502 of the Reckoning, a hairy star, brassy, burned where the day goes down for ten nights, and many feared it.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Skebrae
text: Be it remembered that in the year 507 the moon put on a robe of blood above Skebrae.
In the year of grace 516, the moon put on a robe of blood above Skebrae.
In the year 525, a storm from the sea drove the waves over the shore at Laramirn. A flood of complaints reached the court.
In the year 526, the dikes of Wugoutour gave way and the sea came in.
In the year 528 of the Reckoning, merchants from Brabrox filled the squares of Raewaem with silk and pepper.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Skebrae
text: Be it remembered that in the year 528 Thetynd emptied like a broken jar, and its folk scattered to the hills.
Be it remembered that in the year 529 flames ate the roofs of Raewaem from one gate to the other.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Skebrae
text: Be it remembered that in the year 533 the heavens shut their doors over Aenkov and not a drop fell all summer.
In the year 534 of the Reckoning, a hairy star, brassy, burned towards the setting sun for eleven nights, and many feared it.
In the year 534 of the Reckoning, flames ate the roofs of Hawoumia from one gate to the other. The abbot fell sick in the winter.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Skebrae
text: Be it remembered that in the year 534 flames ate the roofs of Mynyzael from one gate to the other. A two-headed calf was born at Oskdriath.
In the year 549 of the Reckoning, an ember-bright broom of fire swept the heavens above the pole for four nights.
Be it remembered that in the year 562 heaven showed a bearded light, yellow, in the west, which shone twelve nights.
Be it remembered that in the year 576 merchants from Brabrox filled the squares of Simgry with silk and pepper.
Be it remembered that in the year 582 the sun hid its face at noon and the birds fell silent.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Greifel
text: Year 594. Death of Duke Poua.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Greifel
text: That year, 595, the wells of Hawoumia ran dry.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Greifel
text: Year 596. Fire at Hawoumia.
In the year 597 of the Reckoning, a hairy star, honey-coloured, burned over the evening hills for twelve nights, and many feared it.
609. Fair at Simgry.
In the year 621 of the Reckoning, merchants from Brabrox filled the squares of Simgry with silk and pepper. The chronicler's hand grew weary.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Skebrae
text: In the year of grace 622, flames ate the roofs of Simgry from one gate to the other.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Skebrae
text: In the year 626 of the Reckoning, a golden fiery sword hung in the sky where the day goes down for eleven nights. There was hunger for war among the young lords.
In the year of grace 629, want sat at every table in Boudand, and mothers boiled grass for their children.
Be it remembered that in the year 629 want sat at every table in Greifel, and mothers boiled grass for their children.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Skebrae
text: Be it remembered that in the year 632 the sea rose up in anger against Laramirn and the boats were split like kindling.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Skebrae
text: In the year 633 of the Reckoning, the sea tore open the walls of earth at Thetynd and poured its salt upon the fields. There was hunger for war among the young lords.
In the year 634, no rain fell in Stuweisko from spring to autumn.
